newsitem.title: INDIA: India oil refining capacity seen rising by 2001/02.
newsitem.headline: India oil refining capacity seen rising by 2001/02.

text.p: India's annual crude oil refining capacity is expected to rise to 131 million tonnes in the next five years from the current 61 million, with active private sector investment, a company official said on Saturday.

"Plans have been drawn by the oil industry to add another 70 million tonnes per annum refining capacity during the next five years...," R.K. Narang, chairman of state-run Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), told a petroleum technology conference in the Indian capital.

Narang said the refining capacity can be increased by "low cost expansions, debottlenecking of existing refineries, capacity addition through grassroot refineries and investment by the private sector".
He said the annual refining capacity is expected to go up to 173 million tonnes by the year 2006/07.
Narang said demand for petroleum products was growing rapidly in the Asia-Pacific region and the deficit in the region is projected at around 85 million tonnes by 2000.

"Considering India's vast coastline, proximity to the growing demand centres and being enroute from the main source of crude oil -- Middle East -- ample opportunities exist for setting up export-oriented refineries in India," Narang said.

He said IOC's refinery at Panipat in the northern state of Haryana, with an annual capacity of 6.0 million tonnes, was now slated for commissioning next year. It had previously been expected to start up by August this year.
Another IOC refinery in the northeastern state of Assam, with an annual capacity of 3.0 million tonnes, was expected to be operational by 1998/99.
